title: Create sanity-probe & edge-case harness for streaming + function/tool call compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a lightweight, automatable sanity-probe and an edge-case test harness to validate streaming + function/tool-call behavior for newly onboarded models and pinned versions before publishing performance profiles.

Scope:
- Verify non-blocking streaming semantics when a model emits tool call directives mid-stream (partial JSON + trailing tokens).
- Validate recovery and fallback behavior when a downstream tool callback fails (timeouts, 5xx) and ensure the runtime preserves KV cache correctness.
- Surface latency regressions introduced by kernel selection or quantized-code paths when tool-calling interleaves with long KV cache reuse.
- Confirm stream-chunk boundaries do not break structured output parsing for function signatures across different sequence-chunking strategies.

Non-goals:
- Exhaustive performance benchmarking across all model families (this ticket provides quick safety checks only).
- Replacing existing conformance matrix — this is a light, fast probe used in onboarding pipelines and canary gates.

Deliverables:
1) A small test harness runnable in CI and locally that spins a minimal mock tool server and a streaming client harness.
2) A suite of 12 targeted test cases (happy path + 11 edge cases) with deterministic assertions and tolerances.
3) Automation hook that fails onboarding pipeline on high-confidence incompatibilities and uploads a short JSON report to the model onboarding artifact store.
4) Runbook for triage with links to kernel logs, KV cache diffs, and suggested rollback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs headless in CI in under 6 minutes on standard worker

At least 12 test cases implemented covering: partial-token tool calls, tool timeouts, tool 5xx, mid-stream schema flips, KV-cache eviction during stream, backpressure simulation, and tokenizer boundary splits
Onboarding job fails with non-zero code and attaches report when any high-confidence incompatibility is detected
Report schema includes: model-id, pinned-version, test-name, failure-reason, sample-stream, kernel-path, kv-cache-checksum
One-page runbook committed to Drive and linked in ticket
No changes required in production code paths for supported models; harness uses runtime debug hooks already present or adds opt-in probe flags
notes: We should reuse the lightweight mock-tool framework from infra/tests/mock_tools to avoid duplication
Prefer using existing runtime debug flags (runtime.dump-kv and runtime.stream-trace) — if missing, add minimal opt-in hooks rather than invasive changes
Edge-case 'partial JSON then tool call' historically caused parser state loss in r1.18 for some quantized kernels — add targeted regression check against that kernel selection path
We will not run this harness on GPU-heavy canaries by default; CI workers emulate streaming behavior with small model snapshots
If a test requires >1s wall time to reproduce deterministically, mark as flaky and skip in the fast path; surface as a separate nightly job
test_plan_steps: Create mock tool server that can: respond normally, delay past timeout, return 5xx, and return invalid schema
Implement streaming client that can feed prompts with deliberate tokenization boundary traps and capture raw stream frames
Instrument runtime to capture kernel selection metadata and KV cache fingerprints for each stream session
Write deterministic assertions comparing expected vs observed stream shapes, assertion tolerances for latency, and kv-cache checksum equality
Add CI job 'onboard-sanity-probe' invoked by model onboarding pipeline before publishing performance profile
Publish minimal failure report artifact to onboarding-bucket and create console link for the model onboarding PR
